data.message: Retrieving the official financial statement PDF from the CSE document repository
Document secured and staged for processing
Running multi-dimensional financial health diagnostics with LLM (this may take a minute)...
Health diagnostics finalised for DIAL.N0000 — overall score: 82/100 · Good

standardHealthChecks.name: Liquidity Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Current ratio stands at 0.55 (Current Assets: LKR 69.17Bn vs Current Liabilities: LKR 126.14Bn), resulting in a working capital deficit of LKR 56.97Bn. High short-term borrowings (LKR 41.45Bn) weigh on liquidity, though strong operating cash generation mitigates immediate default risks.

standardHealthChecks.name: Profitability Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Profit for the quarter reached LKR 9.19Bn, up 122.5% YoY from LKR 4.13Bn in Q1 2025. Gross profit margin expanded to 56.8% and Net profit margin improved to 19.4%, supported by strong revenue growth of 9.2% YoY to LKR 47.29Bn.

standardHealthChecks.name: Debt Management
standardHealthChecks.description: Total borrowings and lease liabilities stand at LKR 74.83Bn relative to LKR 99.21Bn in equity (Debt-to-Equity of 75.4%). Operating profit (LKR 12.85Bn) provides robust interest coverage of 6.15x against net finance costs.

standardHealthChecks.name: Cash Flow Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Generated LKR 19.82Bn in net operating cash flow for the quarter, easily funding capital expenditures of LKR 6.58Bn and producing solid Free Cash Flow of LKR 13.24Bn.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: EBITDA Margin & Operational Efficiency
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Group EBITDA reached LKR 24.45Bn, translating to a dominant EBITDA margin of 51.7%. This highlights strong scale benefits, cost control, and network efficiency.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: EBITDA margin is a critical benchmark in telecommunications for evaluating core operating profitability prior to heavy non-cash network depreciation and spectrum amortization.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Capital Expenditure Intensity & Infrastructure Reinvestment
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Capex-to-revenue ratio stood at 13.9% (LKR 6.58Bn spent in Q1 2026), with substantial future capex commitments of LKR 19.88Bn secured for continued network expansion.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Telecom service providers require consistent infrastructure reinvestment in 4G/5G, fiber networks, and transmission capacity to maintain quality of service and market share.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Segment Revenue Diversification
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Mobile operations generated LKR 36.43Bn (77.0% of external revenue), supported by Fixed Telephony & Broadband (LKR 6.89Bn / 14.6%) and Digital Television (LKR 3.97Bn / 8.4%).
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Diversification into fixed broadband, enterprise digital solutions, and pay-TV reduces dependence on traditional mobile voice/data revenues.

recommendations: Refinance or restructure short-term debt (LKR 41.45Bn) into longer maturities to improve the current ratio and resolve the working capital deficit.
Maintain disciplined capex deployment toward high-yield 5G/fiber projects as capital commitments expand to LKR 19.88Bn.
Continue growing fixed broadband and digital television segment revenues to further diversify away from core mobile reliance.
Optimize cash balances and short-term payables management to strengthen the quick ratio.
result.analysisNotes: Dialog Axiata PLC demonstrated strong Q1 2026 financial performance, characterized by doubling net profit YoY, expanding EBITDA margins to 51.7%, and generating robust operating cash flows. While working capital remains negative—a feature common to telecom operators with high short-term liabilities—the company's low net debt-to-EBITDA leverage and strong interest coverage ensure high financial stability.
